usage_rules: Every datum carries a source key into the `sources` registry, an as-of date, and a reliability grade.

Reliability grades: A = official published statistic or adopted regulation; B = professional study estimate (survey or model) with known n; C = point-in-time observation, news report, or secondary-source figure pending verification against the primary source; X = placeholder, DO NOT USE until filled.
Grade C and X values may not be quoted in public-facing survey materials. They exist only to mark what needs verification.
When two sources disagree (e.g., ACS median rent vs. 2024 household-survey median rent), the survey must present neither as 'the' rent; it uses the range and names both sources.
ACS estimates whose margin of error exceeds 30% of the estimate are marked moe_unstable:true and may only be used with the MOE shown.
Update cadence: income limits and FMR annually (CHFA ~May, HUD FMR ~Oct 1); ACS each December release; Telluride Guidelines whenever THA amends Appendix A/B.

geography.study_area: San Miguel County, Colorado, with jurisdiction-level detail for Town of Telluride, Town of Mountain Village, Norwood, Ophir, Sawpit/Placerville, and unincorporated county. Regional context (Ridgway, Montrose, Rico) noted where sources include it.
geography.note: Demographic/income statistics are place-of-residence; jobs and wage statistics are place-of-employment. Do not mix the two when computing affordability (per HNA methodology notes).

definitions.affordable: Housing costing no more than 30% of gross household income. Renters: rent + utilities. Owners: principal, interest, taxes, insurance. (HUD standard; HNA glossary.)
definitions.cost_burdened: Paying more than 30% of gross income for housing. Severely cost burdened: more than 50%.
definitions.ami: Area Median Income for San Miguel County, published annually by HUD and CHFA, varies by household size. The Town of Telluride adopts its own AMI table in Guidelines Appendix A.
definitions.gross_rent_vs_contract_rent: ACS 'gross rent' = contract rent + estimated utilities. Survey questions must specify whether a reported rent includes utilities; Telluride Maximum Rental Rates are quoted INCLUDING utilities, less a utility allowance.
definitions.market_rate: Housing with no deed restriction on price, rent, use, or occupancy.
definitions.deed_restricted: Housing with recorded restrictions on rent/sale price, occupancy, and/or income eligibility.
definitions.telluride_tiers: Town of Telluride income-eligibility tiers. Tier 1 targets ~70-90% AMI; Tier 2 ~90-110%; Tier 3 (legacy, no longer created) ~80-100% targets with 130% cap; Tier 4 ~130-150% targets. Eligibility caps: Tier 1 = 120% of household-size AMI, Tier 2 = 180%, Tier 3 = 130%.
definitions.fmr: HUD Fair Market Rent: 40th-percentile gross rent for a standard-quality unit, set annually per county. Governs Housing Choice Voucher payment standards. It is a RENT STANDARD, not a market median.

chfa_2025_san_miguel_county.note: Rural resort county: Prop 123 tiers extend to 160% AMI. 100% AMI 4-person = $119,500. Max rents assume 1.5 persons/bedroom and include utility allowance per LIHTC convention.

tha_2025_appendix_a.note: The Town of Telluride's adopted AMI grid (Appendix A) — matches the CHFA 2025 vintage (100% 1p $83,700). The 130% / 4-person figure is printed as $155.350 in the PDF — an obvious typo for $155,350, recorded as corrected. Printed 120% row does not exactly equal 1.2 x 100% row ($100,400 vs computed $100,440); the printed value governs. NOTE: with CHFA 2026 limits now ~9.7% higher, expect THA to update this grid; watch for an amendment.

caveats: Superseded by acs_median_gross_rent_2020_2024 below; retained for trend.
5-year pooled estimates lag the market; small-geography MOEs are large; the informal market is undercounted.

interpretation: Telluride's median gross rent JUMPED to $3,056 (±359) from $1,844 in the 2018-2022 vintage — the post-2021 market repricing is now visible in federal data.

The COUNTY median ($1,149) is now BELOW the 2018-2022 county median ($1,267) because Mountain Village's 1,134 renter households (mostly deed-restricted, median $1,072) dominate the countywide renter universe of 1,705.
Lesson for the survey: countywide medians hide everything; always split by jurisdiction and restriction status.

acs_median_gross_rent_by_bedrooms_2020_2.interpretation: County 0-2BR medians ($789-$1,162) sit at deed-restricted price points; 3BR ($2,742) is where the market-rate segment shows. The bedroom split is the cleanest public evidence that the rental market is two different markets.

rent_burden_2020_2024.table: B25070 (gross rent as % of household income)

san_miguel_county.note: Over half of county renters are cost-burdened by the HUD 30% standard; over a third severely. The 50%+ MOE is very wide (±342 on 594) — quote as 'roughly a third' with the MOE, never as a precise figure.

telluride.note: 48 of 178 'not computed' — tiny universe, unusable for burden shares; use county figures.

household_survey_2024_reported_rent.regime_change_warning: Fielded September 2024 — BEFORE the Town of Telluride's January 2025 income-based rent rules took effect at town-managed properties (see town_managed_rentals). Deed-restricted rents reported here do not reflect post-2025 income-linked rents. Any new survey must date-stamp rent questions and ask about rent changes since January 2025.

hud_fair_market_rents.interpretation: FY2026 FMRs DROPPED ~6-8% across all sizes (2BR $1,743 -> $1,645) because HUD's FY2026 base moved to ACS 2019-2023, in which the county's deed-restricted-heavy renter mix pulls the 40th percentile down. An FMR decrease in one of Colorado's least affordable rental markets is itself a finding about how badly standard statistics capture this market — a fair survey should note it, not hide it.

point_in_time_listings_2025.caveat: Anecdotal, n=5. Illustrates the listed-market vs. paid-rent gap; NEVER quote as a market statistic. Useful only to justify the structured listing audit.

agency_listings_snapshot_2026_07.note: Everything the region's housing agencies had publicly listed on this date, via the Livable Telluride housing page. Key validation: the one active deed-restricted rental listing ($1,883/mo room) exactly equals the THA Tier 2 studio/1BR Maximum Rental Rate — the Guidelines formula is binding in practice.
agency_listings_snapshot_2026_07.interpretation: On any given day the entire publicly listed deed-restricted rental market is essentially one room plus three waitlists (one capped). 'What's available' and 'what people pay' are different questions — the survey must ask both.

regional_out_commute_acs_2020_2024.note: Where Telluride's workforce actually out-commutes from. Ridgway ~45 min / Montrose ~70 min to Telluride. Montrose 1BR medians are skewed low by subsidized/senior stock (huge MOEs) — anchor on 2BR/3BR, which are the county's most reliable rent statistics in this entire file (MOE under 7%).

all.note: MOE equals the estimate — DO NOT USE; use ouray_county

1br.note: skewed by subsidized stock — do not use

regional_out_commute_acs_2020_2024.commute_context: HNA: in-commuters are a major share of the Telluride workforce; households outside SMC saw housing costs rise 77% (~$900/mo) since 2011 vs 35% inside SMC [RRC24].

deed_restricted_max_rents_telluride.formula: Maximum Rental Rate = 30% of the tier's target income / 12, quoted INCLUDING utilities, charged as rent less a utility allowance (HUD Utility Allowance). Verified: Tier 1 studio $1,465 = 30% x $58,590 (70% of 1-person AMI) / 12.
deed_restricted_max_rents_telluride.fees_rule: Max rents may not be increased by additional fees. Landlord may separately charge actual utilities up to 20% of the Maximum Rental Rate, or per HUD Utility Allowance (Guidelines s.207).

tier_3.note: Legacy tier; units with permission to rent follow the Tier 1 rental standard.

deed_restricted_max_rents_telluride.room_rentals: A room in a Tier 1 or Tier 3 unit rents at the Tier 1 studio/1BR max; a room in a Tier 2 or Tier 4 unit rents at the Tier 2 studio/1BR max.
deed_restricted_max_rents_telluride.scope_caveat: These are TOWN OF TELLURIDE deed-restriction rules (mitigation units, EDUs, etc.). Town-MANAGED apartment complexes (Shandoka, Sunnyside, Voodoo, Boarding House) run on a separate income-based system — see town_managed_rentals. SMRHA (county), Mountain Village, and Norwood programs also have separate schedules — see download_list.

vca_rents_2026.note: Actual adopted rents at Village Court Apartments — the county's largest rental complex. These supersede the ACS-based MV estimates for program purposes. Explains the ACS MV medians almost exactly (ACS 0BR $786 / 1BR $1,116 / 2BR $1,154 vs. these schedules).
vca_rents_2026.eligibility: Tenants must be employed (or show intent to be employed) within the Telluride R-1 School District per the MV Employee Housing Restriction (Ord. 1997-05). Retiree exception: 60+ with R-1 employment history.

terms.min_occupancy: one person per bedroom (a single person cannot rent a 2BR)
terms.utilities: Rent includes water, sewer, trash, recycling. Electricity separately metered and tenant-paid (SMPA or Fair Energy depending on unit type).
terms.pets: Dogs allowed: $300 refundable deposit + $30/month; cats $300 deposit.
terms.fees: Application $50/adult; admin $50 + $10 per additional earner; parking pass $50/vehicle one-time.

town_managed_rentals.reliability: A for inventory and eligibility; C for rent-rule effects (news-sourced) pending Town confirmation

sunnyside.units: 8 townhomes + 3 tiny homes + 18 apartments + in-home daycare

inventory.eligibility: Year-round housing for employees working within the Telluride R-1 School District boundaries. Waitlist-based; town-employee priority on some properties. Contact rentalhousing@telluride.gov / (970) 728-4025.
inventory.rent_calculator: Town publishes a '2026 Rent Calculator' and 'Employee Rental Housing Policies' document on the page above — the authoritative rent formula lives there.

rent_system_verified_2026.formula: Rent = (AMI Rent Target income for the household's TIER and SIZE) / 12 x project multiplier x unit-amenities multiplier. Rent is pegged to the tier's target income, not the household's exact income — effective burden runs ~20-25% of gross within a tier and steps up at tier boundaries (renewal income documentation drives tier reassignment; this is the mechanism behind the reported big rent jumps).

income_tiers.note: Tier = rent target %AMI / income limit %AMI. A household qualifies for the lowest tier whose limit covers its income.
income_tiers.initial_lease_cap: No initial leases in Tiers H-J; households may only ADVANCE into them at renewal.

rent_system_verified_2026.ami_tables: Leases before 2026-01-01 use April 2024 AMI; on/after use April 2025 AMI (2-person 100% = $95,600 — matches THA Appendix A).

shandoka_a_e_2026_rates_verified.note: From the live calculator; unit counts in parentheses. Tier A -> J.

rent_system_verified_2026.eligibility_standards: Employed in R-1 district; primary residence; NO ownership of developed residential property in San Miguel/Montrose/Ouray/Dolores counties; net-asset limits by tier (Tier A: 10x the 45%-AMI income ... Tier J: 5x the 220%-AMI income); minimum household size = bedrooms (2BR needs 2 people); minimum income 2x monthly rent; verified deductions (childcare/medical/retirement/education/FHSA) capped at $15,000 per adult.
rent_system_verified_2026.monthly_admin_fees: Electricity administration $30/mo + water/sewer administration $30/mo (Appendix D) — add to rent when normalizing gross housing cost.

voodoo.note: Appendix E lists 8 studios/0 1BR; the 2025 Voodoo AMI-limits rent table (lottery document) splits them 6 studios + 2 one-bedrooms — the lottery table governs

property_rent_tables_2025.source: Official TOT AMI-Limits/Rent tables 2025, all four properties, archived in assets/Housing Study/Units and rents 2026/ (Voodoo, Shandoka, Sunnyside, Virginia Placer PDFs). Basis: Rental Housing Policies adopted 2024-11-19; 2024 AMI grid; pre-2026 multipliers (27%/30%).

voodoo.post_occupancy_income_cap: 220% AMI (THA); grant-assisted units 110-150% per grant covenant

initial_qualification_caps_by_property.note: The cheapest option (Shandoka A-E at the lowest multiplier) is closed to NEW tenants above Tier D (120% AMI limit); mid-tier households enter through Sunnyside/Bldg F/Voodoo at higher rents. Sunnyside has no Tier A/B rents at all — its floor is the 80%-AMI-target rent.

voodoo_unit_mix_and_initial_rents_2024_l.notes: Rents set below state (DOLA covenant) maximums; utilities charged to tenant on top, with landlord absorbing any excess over state caps (Lease 18.5). This table is the grade-A documentation of the 110-170% AMI product positioning.

bldg_f_12_units_listed.discrepancy: Policies App. E lists Bldg F at 29 units — unresolved; rent table may list unit TYPES only. Verify with THD.

a_e_g_h_111_units.note: 2025 rates (2024 AMI x 27%); superseded by 2026 rates (2025 AMI x 25%) — e.g. 1BR Tier A $777 -> $785

virginia_placer_2025_rates.note: Rent table lists 4 studios vs App. E's 6 — minor discrepancy, verify with THD

sunnyside_2025_rates.note: 2BR C $1,808 = 80%-target x 2-person 2024 AMI x 30%/12 + rounding conventions; Sunnyside multiplier 30% in 2025, 27% from 2026-01-01

notes: Example rent trajectories reported by tenants under the income-based system: Shandoka 3BR $1,800 -> $2,400 -> $3,600; Sunnyside 4BR $2,450 -> $2,850 -> $4,400.
~49 town units vacant April 2026 (~25% of the complexes then counted).
Minimum work requirement reported reduced 1,400 -> 1,200 hrs/yr in town (verify against Policies section 103).

town_managed_rentals.survey_relevance: This is the single most consequential recent change in local rental economics, and it post-dates every dataset above except ACS tail-end. The survey MUST distinguish town-managed income-based rent from deed-restricted flat-max rent from market rent, and ask when the respondent's rent last changed.

rental_affordability.note: For 2026-dollar equivalents, recompute from chfa_2026_san_miguel_county (30% of income / 12) rather than inflating these.

monthly_gap_to_median_market_rent_1848.note: Positive = subsidy needed to reach the $1,848 market-rate median (2024 household survey).

arts_entertainment_rec_71.note: includes ski operations — the county's 2nd-largest sector

affordability_bridge.note: Affordable monthly rent = annual pay x 0.30 / 12, single-earner household.
affordability_bridge.vs: 2024 survey market-rate median rent $1,848; FY2026 FMR 1BR $1,254; Telluride ACS median $3,056. A single average tourism-sector earner cannot afford the market-rate median anywhere in the county without roommates.

amenities_baseline.note: What public data actually supports about the amenities a renter can expect. Anchors survey questions about unit size, condition, and what rent includes.

renter_bedrooms_acs_2020_2024.note: ACS shows more studios (20%) than the 2024 survey (9%) — the survey under-reached dorm/studio dwellers; weight accordingly.

utilities_convention.rule: Deed-restricted max rents include utilities (less allowance); market listings typically EXCLUDE utilities. Survey must ask 'does your rent include heat / electricity / internet?' and normalize to gross rent before comparison.
utilities_convention.scope_note: Per maintainer (2026-07-31): the survey does NOT model utility rates. It only asks whether rent includes utilities and, if not, roughly what the respondent pays per month. No tariff data belongs in this file.

structure_and_condition.needed: Furnished/unfurnished, pets, parking, lease length, W/D, condition — no government source records these. Filled only by the listing audit (template: listing-audit-template.csv in this folder).

telluride.note: Startlingly low — town renters largely live in MV, Lawson Hill, or town-managed units counted oddly; reconcile before quoting.

mountain_village.note: 73% of MV's occupied units are renter-occupied — MV is the county's rental hub.

households_in_temporary_housing.caveat: likely undercount (survey-distribution and disclosure-fear bias, per HNA)

top_reasons_for_moving_smc_pct.note: 'Owner sold the rental unit' was the most common reason (over a third of SMC movers, per HNA ch.6 narrative; exact row not re-extracted).

ownership_market_context.note: Context only — the survey is rental-focused, but these anchor the 'could you ever buy here?' framing.
ownership_market_context.income_needed_for_median_unit: Telluride median sale price requires ~850-960% AMI household income (HNA Table 18).

sales_below_200pct_ami_affordability_202.note: Only ~20% of 2024 sales (through August) were affordable below 200% AMI.

median_owner_occupied_value_acs_2020_202.note: ACS self-reported value, dragged down by deed-restricted stock — 6.3x below the MLS single-family median. Another two-markets illustration.

survey_statistical_targets.note: Statistical-validity yardsticks for the Livable Telluride survey, derived from this baseline.

population_frames.note: ACS 2020-2024 frames (grade A) supersede the 0.1.0 survey-derived estimates (3,998 / ~1,360).

sample_size_for_95conf_5moe.method: finite-population correction, p=0.5, recomputed on ACS frames

survey_statistical_targets.benchmark: The 2024 RRC regional survey achieved n=1,129 total / 821 SMC / 338 renters — treat those as the bar for credibility.
design_rules_from_baseline: Rent-amount answer bands must be built from this file's breakpoints (FMR, tier max rents, CHFA 2026 rent limits, affordable-rent-by-AMI), not round guesses.
Always ask utilities-included yes/no and normalize to gross rent.
Ask market vs. deed-restricted vs. town-managed income-based vs. employer-provided — FOUR populations with different baselines.
Date-stamp rent answers and ask about changes since January 2025 (town-managed regime change).
Report results against the baseline range (ACS county $1,149 ... survey market-rate $1,848 ... Telluride ACS $3,056), never a single 'true rent'.
Weight or at least report by jurisdiction; Mountain Village holds 2/3 of the county's renters and skews every countywide number.
